chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Kahili, who said:
I asked him about tayammum. He said: He struck the carpet with his hand, then wiped his face with it, then wiped his two palms, one of them over the back of the other.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution performed in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath) under specific conditions
key_terms.الْبِسَاطِ: the carpet or spread surface upon which the hand was struck
key_terms.ظَهْرِ: the back part of the hand over which the other hand is wiped
key_terms.فَضَرَبَ: he struck or placed the hand upon a surface for beginning tayammum
key_terms.كَفَّيْهِ: his two palms or hands, which are wiped as part of tayammum
key_terms.وَجْهَهُ: his face, which is wiped in the procedure of tayammum

ai.seo_question: How is tayammum performed according to the hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the manner of tayammum in a concise practical form. It shows striking the surface, wiping the face, and then wiping the hands, making it an important narration in the jurisprudence of ritual purity and worship.
